name: ethernet-board-pnr
prompt: My Ethernet PHY board's constraints are in the design and nothing is placed yet. Place and route the board in the open layout so I can keep editing it in the board editor.

inputs.project: A JITX project whose design, ethboard.main.EthernetBoardDesign, holds jitxexamples.jumpstart_kits.js2_circuits.main.EthernetPhyBoard (TPS62933 buck from 12 V to 3.3 V, KSZ9031RNX PHY with its core LDO MOSFET, 25 MHz crystal, straps, LED resistors and decoupling, Bel Fuse 0826-1G1T-23-F RJ45 jack with integrated magnetics and LEDs, four center-tap capacitors and the MDIO pull-up) plus a Weidmuller LSF-SMT 2-pole terminal block on VIN and GND and a Samtec TSW-110-07-T-D 2 x 10 header whose pins 2, 9, 19 and 20 are GND and whose other 16 pins each can take any of the 16 host signals (RGMII TX and RX, MDC, MDIO, RESET_N, INT_N) through provide/require pin assignment. The board is 80 x 40 mm (ethboard.substrate.EthernetBoardOutline) on ethboard.substrate.EthernetBoardSubstrate, the 18-layer jitxexamples.substrates.reference_18layer stackup offering only two through-hole via definitions (TOP to BOTTOM, 6.0 and 10.0 mil drill), neither allowing via-in-pad, each with a delay model for every pair of layers it joins so a timed route through either is measured. The design source carries the constraints: board default width and clearance 0.125 mm, thermal relief, a 0.5 mm width rule at priority 1 on VIN, V3V3, V1V2 (the LDO MOSFET's output to the PHY core) and GND, the buck circuit's own 0.25 mm rule on its VIN and VOUT and 0.25 mm clearance on its switch and bootstrap nets, the four MDI pairs on DRS_100_L3 (100 ohm, coupled on L3_SIG1 only, uncoupled region on TOP and L3_SIG1 with 0.2 mm clearance) with GND reference and an intra-pair skew limit of +/-0.8 ps, every host net on SE_50_TOP (50 ohm, TOP only), RGMII TX data and TX_CTL against TXC and RX data and RX_CTL against RXC within +/-200 ps from the header pin to the PHY pin, ShortTrace on XI and XO to the crystal, a 0.375 mm clearance rule from XI and XO traces to every trace of any other net except each other, and to ISET copper, GND pours on L2, L4, L6, L8, L11, L13, L15 and L17, and a V3V3 pour on L9_PWR1_2OZ over the board's signal area. The module docstring of ethboard/main.py states each number with its source. No component is placed in code and nothing is routed. Copy the project to a scratch directory; never run against the user's own checkout. The project's `[tool.jitx.parts] chain` is `["csv:parts/example-passives.csv", "ideal"]`, with the kit catalogue in `parts/`; a build that resolves any part to an `IDEAL-` placeholder makes the case invalid.
inputs.environment: The JITX CLI and runtime installed at the bundle's supported version line (see the base jitx skill); the runner starts its own runtime and session for the copy and stops the session at the end. The project's substrate, jitxexamples.substrates.reference_18layer, is in no jitxexamples release through 2.1.0, only in pre-release builds, so this case needs such a build beside the supported versions; on the released packages alone the project does not build and the case does not run.
inputs.notes: Another full board with an input connector, a switching regulator feeding an inner power plane, a QFN consumer with decoupling, a crystal, a pin-assigned host connector and a high-speed connector with differential pairs, the same constraint set in the source and through-hole vias only, is an equivalent fixture.

notes: For whoever reads the judges' output, not for the runner. The case tests the whole playbook on a complete board: floorplan with the connectors on edges and blocks along the flow of power and signals, dense and organized local placement that keeps routes short, the buck's tight loops first with its capacitors turned toward the IC and inductor, plane vias, then the bulk; and it tests that the SI constraints in the source are met, not only present. The board is 80 x 40 mm; the jack's courtyard is about 20 x 35 mm with the depth perpendicular to its cable face, so with the cable face on any edge its depth runs into the board. Courtyards total 1331.8 mm^2 against 3200 mm^2 of board (0.42), measured on the fixture build. Vias are through-hole only and the via definitions forbid via-in-pad, so a ground or power pad reaches a plane through a via beside the pad on a short stub. The power path under test runs terminal block, input capacitors, buck, inductor, output capacitors, vias into the V3V3 plane on L9_PWR1_2OZ, and vias out of it at each 3.3 V consumer. The V3V3 pour has no pad on its layer until a via reaches it, so it reads as empty at the start; a final state where it is still empty, or in more than one piece, means the plane was not fed. The 0.5 mm power rule is wider than the TPS62933's 0.28 mm pads and the PHY's 0.30 mm QFN pads; a default-width route into such a pad came back routed with about 0.11 mm to its neighbours and rd.issues() reported nothing (probed 2026-11-05), so a cited neck-down at the pad is following the skill and a default-width route there is a silent clearance violation. The SI constraints were each shown live while building the fixture: a routed MDI pair reported a Skew issue against +/-800 fs and a routed TXD0/TXC pair a Skew issue against +/-200 ps; with nothing routed every constraint reports 'No path for signal constraint'. A final issue list that still shows that topology error (ERROR severity), or a Skew error, means a constraint was not met. Each constraint was also shown achievable on this fixture: one MDI pair on L3_SIG1 through two through-hole vias reached 75.5 fs (untuned 2.2 ps) after its via was moved 0.45 mm (its insertion legs routed at 0.2 mm space, now the structure's uncoupled clearance; at the reference's 0.264 mm they blocked), and the full RX group with its strap stubs on TOP read satisfied, worst 82.6 ps against +/-200 ps. The header pin assignment chosen at the first build need not be routable on one layer once parts are placed; a route request to another pool pin does not re-solve it, and restarting the session after placement did re-solve it against the placement in that probe. The crystal's ShortTrace and clearance rule produce no issue of their own, and state.json carries no trace geometry, so the runner's own clearance measurement is the only evidence for the crystal clearance; XI against XO is exempt from the rule (their pads, 45 and 46, are 0.5 mm apart). The host nets' routing structure, SE_50_TOP, covers TOP only; whether the runtime flags a host route on another layer was not shown while building the fixture, so the judge reads the layers from state.json. The header's pin choice is pin-assigned, so the runner states which header pin each host signal took; the jack's pair-to-pin assignment is pin-assigned too (MDI1000BaseT require on the jack). The jack's cable face is +y in its own frame (shield pads p17 and p18 at y = +8.6 mm, the pin rows at negative y); placed on the top side at rotation r degrees CCW, it faces r + 90 degrees, and that direction must point off the nearest board edge. The terminal block is top entry and the header vertical, so for them only the edge position is judged. The jack's SHIELD pads form their own net with no board connection, left for the enclosure: tying them to GND is not asked and is a change of intent the summary must flag. The jack has integrated magnetics and terminations, so the board has no cable-side copper and no isolation gap is asked. The circuitousness limit is the user's: a routed connection never longer than 1.5 times the straight line between its ends, closer to 1 better. Run e1 (2026-11-05, 80 x 80 board, before these changes) is the failure picture: its bulk input capacitors' loops measured 10.5 and 17.2 mm^2 against 0.94 mm^2 for the 100 nF capacitor, a 0.25 mm VIN trace sat between an input capacitor and the buck against the 0.5 mm rule, LED1.c (jack pin 13 to PHY pin 17, with a strap resistor on it) ran 1.6 times its straight line, and the LDO MOSFET was routed thin and indirect. The hot-loop target has no datasheet number; the runner states the target it used and why. The 4x bound against the 100 nF capacitor's loop in the loop assertion is the case's choice, not a sourced figure: bulk parts are larger, so some ratio above 1 is honest packing, and e1's 11x and 18x are well past it. Power paths are judged by layout_checks.py's estimated DC IR drop at a current against a drop budget, and its coarse inductance estimate (l_nh) against an inductance budget, not by the narrowest point: thermal spokes, necks and traces count by the resistance they add. The runner takes the current from the design source (the circuit's rating or load) or states it with its reason, and states the budget with its reason; the case sets neither. The 'input is a pour' requirement (`require_pour`, trace_hops 0) is separate from the drop: in e1 the VIN path from the terminal block to the buck, with 20.3 mm of trace legs, was estimated at 11.1 mOhm, 11.1 mV at 1 A, which a 1% budget would pass, so the pour requirement is what carries that fault. Evidence: the judges read the final layout from the last layout_report.py and layout_checks.py outputs in the transcript, the archived project (its .jitx/interactive-layout/ files when present), the harness-project.diff the harness writes after the run (every change to the scratch project against its baseline), and the runner's scripts. A claim in COMPLETION.md counts only where that evidence backs it; a claim it contradicts is a false claim. The prompt says no more than a user would: the layer plan (MDI on L3_SIG1, host nets on TOP), the header pin assignment, the planes and the crystal rules are all in the design source, so the runner finds them there. Run e2 (2026-11-06) broke the MDI pairs out on TOP from the jack's through-hole pads to vias instead of leaving the pads on L3_SIG1; run e3 left the jack past the board edge. The 1.5 circuitousness bound is the skill's own standard, not the user's. Runs e4 and e5 (2026-11-06) ran on a fixture whose vias had no delay model, so their MDI skew read placeholders through the vias; a fault there in the MDI skew is the fixture's, not the runner's. The fixture's block circuits (board, board.jack, j_pwr, host) are `.at(floating=True)` in ethboard/main.py; components placed inside a floating circuit lose their placement on a session restart, so the runner is expected to give each block's circuit a placement in the source at its floorplan origin before placing its parts (visible in harness-project.diff).
runner_rationale: Customers drive this skill with mixed-strength agents (Claude Code, Codex, and Devin among them). The skill must carry the mechanics and the checks itself, so the eval runs it under a codex workhorse-tier runner at high effort. Judges stay frontier-tier regardless of runner.
runner_artifacts: Put any scripts you write under <output>/scripts/. When you are done, write me a short note in <output>/COMPLETION.md: what you did and what is left.
expected_output: Re-runnable scripts that floorplan the 80 x 40 mm board (terminal block, RJ45 jack and host header on board edges; the buck between the input connector and the PHY; the PHY between the jack and the header with its crystal, LDO parts and decoupling around it), place each local circuit densely and in order with clear courtyards so each connection's route stays near its straight-line length (each strap resistor on the path between the PHY pin and the jack or header pin it sits on, the LED resistors between the jack's LED anodes and V3V3), place the buck's input and output capacitors with the pads that close each loop facing the IC pins and inductor, route the buck's tight loops first (switch node and bootstrap on the top layer or as a hull pour, the input hot loop joined by region pours), carry 12 V from the terminal block through the input capacitors to the buck as a pour with its IR drop within a stated budget, feed the V3V3 plane from the buck's output capacitors through several through-hole vias, drop each 3.3 V consumer pin and decoupling capacitor to the plane through its own via beside the pad, take every ground pin and capacitor return to a GND plane through a nearby via, route the LDO MOSFET at the power width and direct, route the four MDI pairs as coupled pairs on L3_SIG1 from the PHY to the jack pads the runner chose, matched within the skew limit, route every host net on TOP to header pins chosen through the pin assignment with the RGMII groups within their skew limit, keep XI and XO short and clear of other traces; a read-back and layout_checks.py after each batch; a final state with every component placed on the board, no courtyard overlap, no blocked route, no error issue with every category complete (every SI constraint satisfied), every pour one piece, no connection over 1.5 times its straight line, every power path's IR drop within its stated budget, and a connectivity check over every net written by the runner.

assertions.text: every placement, route, via and pour is made with rd.layout requests from scripts run by jitx design exec; harness-project.diff shows no new Route, via, Copper, Pour, tag, rule or placement in the design's Python source; changes under designs/<design>/design-info/ are expected

the final state has no unplaced component, no courtyard overlap, nothing past the board edge (or each overhang named in COMPLETION.md with its reason, such as a connector lip), no ideal part, no blocked route, no split, empty or fill_unknown pour, and no error-severity issue with every category complete; in particular no 'No path for signal constraint' topology issue and no Skew error remains

the 12 V terminal block, the RJ45 jack and the host header each have a courtyard edge at the board outline, judged from their courtyards and the board outline; the RJ45 jack's cable face points off that edge (see notes for its frame) and the jack's courtyard is inside the board apart from a named lip
every net's pads are joined in the final state, shown by a connectivity check run on the final layout (the skill's or the runner's own) and not contradicted by any other evidence

the input current path from the terminal block's VIN pad through the buck's input capacitors to the buck's VIN pin is a pour made with region requests (GND may return through the GND planes), and a layout_checks.py run on the final layout has a VIN power path from the terminal block to the buck with `require_pour`, trace_hops 0, and an IR drop (r_mohm and drop_mv) within a budget at a current the runner states with its source or reason; only a step-down leg into a pad narrower than the rule, within neck_down_mm of it, may be a trace

the buck's input hot loop pads (the input capacitors' ground pads with the IC's ground pins, and their supply pads with the IC's supply pin) are joined by pours made with region requests, each one fill piece, unless the runner shows why such a pour could not be built in one piece; the switch node and bootstrap connections are short top-layer routes or a hull pour, and any hull pour has a distinct rank and an expand
the buck output reaches the V3V3 plane through more than one via placed at or next to the output capacitors, and the V3V3 pour ends with one fill piece

every 3.3 V consumer pin on the PHY and every decoupling capacitor on V3V3 reaches the plane through a via of its own at or next to its pad, unless the runner names a shared via and shows the shared route is short and the current within what one via carries by the design's rules

every ground pin and every capacitor's ground pad reaches a GND plane through a nearby via (a through-hole ground pad joins the planes through its own barrel), with more than one via on each bulk input and output capacitor of the buck; each capacitor's plane vias sit beside its pads on one side of the part, not past its ends; no ground pad depends on a long surface route to reach the plane

the four MDI pairs are routed as coupled pairs (pair insertions or pair routes) from the PHY to the jack with their coupled length on L3_SIG1; at the jack each leg leaves its through-hole pad on L3_SIG1 at the pad, with no TOP stub to a via; the only MDI vias are at the PHY's top-side pads; the final issue list reports each pair's intra-pair skew within +/-0.8 ps; no MDI leg is routed as two independent single-ended traces

every via serves an end pad: it sits next to the pad it escapes or drops to a plane, never mid-route, and joins copper on at least two layers; a connection uses no more vias than its ends need (0 when both ends reach its layer, 1 when one does not, 2 when neither does)

every VIN, V3V3 or GND trace that ends on a TPS62933 pin (0.28 mm pads) or a PHY QFN signal-row pin (0.30 mm pads; the QFN's GND thermal pad is excluded) is narrowed on the leg that ends at the pad to no wider than the pad, judged from the width set on the request in the scripts, or is measured at least 0.125 mm from the neighbouring pads by a script that reads the trace copper; a 0.5 mm trace into such a pad fails

every host net (RGMII TX and RX, MDC, MDIO, RESET_N, INT_N) is routed on TOP only, with no via on any host net, to header pins chosen through the pin assignment; the final issue list reports both RGMII skew constraints (TX group against TXC, RX group against RXC) satisfied within +/-200 ps

XI and XO each run from the PHY pin to the crystal pad as a short, direct top-layer route with no via, and the crystal and its load capacitors sit next to the PHY's XI and XO pins; if any measurement in the run shows a trace of another net, or ISET copper, within 0.375 mm of an XI or XO trace, this fails

a layout_checks.py run on the final layout shows no routed connection outside the SI nets over 1.5 times its straight-line length, however short (a decoupling capacitor turned so its route loops back to the pin it serves is the kind of fault this catches); any unmeasured route is named

the buck's input and output capacitors are placed with the pads that close each loop facing the IC's VIN and GND pins and the inductor, packed tight in rows or columns rather than scattered, and a layout_checks.py run on the final layout reports each input capacitor's loop area against a target the runner states with its reason, each met; a bulk input capacitor turned away from the IC, a loop not met, or a bulk loop more than 4 times the 100 nF capacitor's (the case's choice, see notes) fails

no via sits inside or overlaps a pad (the via definitions forbid via-in-pad), and no via is placed with force=True unless the scripts first check the spot against pads, large courtyards and neighbouring routes

a layout_checks.py run on the final layout has a V3V3 power path from a buck output capacitor to a PHY 3.3 V pin with its estimated r_mohm, drop_mv and l_nh within budgets the runner states with their reasons; the LDO MOSFET's drain, source and the V1V2 path to the PHY's core pins are routed at the 0.5 mm power width (the design's rule on V3V3 and V1V2) or as pours, direct, with any narrowing at a pad justified

COMPLETION.md says what was done and what is left, shortfalls first; it claims nothing the final state contradicts, and it does not call the board done while any assertion-level fault above (an off-board part, an unrouted net, an error issue, a failed check) remains

each block circuit the fixture leaves floating is given a placement in the source (at its floorplan origin) before its parts are placed, so placements survive a session restart; a run that instead re-places parts after each restart from its own saved file, or leaves the circuits floating, fails
